name: Scott Shepard
identity: Scott R. Shepard, MD — Associate Professor of Clinical Neurosurgery, Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University; Director of Neurosurgical Oncology, Temple University Hospital, Philadelphia PA. Confirmed via NPI 1346359841 and Temple Health directory.
bio: Scott Shepard leads neurosurgical oncology at Temple University Hospital, focusing on brain tumors, brain metastases, and skull lesions treated with a combination of open surgery, stereotactic/Gamma Knife radiosurgery, and laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT). He is Temple's public-facing spokesperson for LITT, having discussed the minimally invasive laser approach for seizure foci and hard-to-reach tumors in Temple Health's 'Moves in Medicine' and 6abc Action News segments. Claims data show him performing LITT on Monteris NeuroBlate for brain metastases, a high-volume metastasis practice. He came to Temple from UT Houston/Memorial Hermann after fellowship at Memorial Sloan Kettering.
training: Weill Cornell Medical College (MD) · General surgery internship NewYork-Presbyterian, neurosurgery residency UC San Francisco · Surgical neuro-oncology fellowship Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center · Strong onc pedigree (UCSF residency + MSKCC surgical neuro-onc).
litt_exposure: Strong. Claims show LITT performed on NeuroBlate (litt_perf=1) within a high-volume brain-metastasis practice (mets_rn=70). Publicly promotes LITT for tumors and epilepsy foci in Temple Health / 6abc media as institutional LITT spokesperson.
wheelhouse: Neurosurgical oncology, brain metastases, primary brain tumors, stereotactic/Gamma Knife radiosurgery, LITT for tumors, neurosurgical critical care.
kol_note: Institutional-level KOL: Director of Neurosurgical Oncology and Temple's media spokesperson for LITT. Influence is clinical/programmatic and regional; verifiable peer-reviewed first-author output appears thin (note: 'Shepard SR' brain-mets/SRS papers in search results trace to Matthew Shepard at UVA, a different person — not attributed here).
flags: Publication record unverified/thin; did NOT attribute Matthew Shepard (UVA) papers to him.
Ours (NeuroBlate) — protect/grow account; already an active user and advocate.

name: Willard Kasoff
identity: Willard Stein Kasoff, MD, MPH — Associate Professor of Neurosurgery, Lewis Katz School of Medicine; Director of Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgery, Temple University Hospital, Philadelphia PA. Packet NPI was null; NPI 1225214166 recovered from public directories (healthcare4ppl/NPPES). bio: Willard Kasoff directs stereotactic and functional neurosurgery at Temple, specializing in surgery for complex disorders of brain function — epilepsy, movement disorders (Parkinson's, essential tremor, dystonia), and pain — including deep brain stimulation and epilepsy surgery. His epilepsy/functional practice (SEEG-guided workup, mesial temporal and lesional ablation) makes him a natural LITT operator, and he is part of Temple's Comprehensive Epilepsy Center multidisciplinary team. He trained in epilepsy and functional/stereotactic neurosurgery at Yale and Emory. A 2024 CV appears in an FDA advisory-panel document, indicating regulatory/advisory engagement.
training: Albert Einstein College of Medicine (MD, with distinction in epilepsy research; also MPH in health policy) · Neurological surgery residency Yale-New Haven / Yale School of Medicine · Fellowship in functional & stereotactic neurosurgery and epilepsy, Emory University School of Medicine (with Yale epilepsy-surgery training) · Functional/epilepsy pedigree (Yale + Emory).

Platform (NeuroBlate vs. Visualase) undetermined.

name: Eric Quach
identity: Eric T. Quach, MD — cerebrovascular/endovascular and skull base neurosurgeon, Temple University Hospital, Philadelphia PA. Confirmed via NPI 1871974469 (matches both packet records). Two packet records ('Eric Quach' Performer + 'Eric T Quach' Development target, same NPI) merged to one person.
bio: Eric Quach is an early-career Temple neurosurgeon specializing in open and endovascular cerebrovascular disease — brain aneurysms, subarachnoid hemorrhage, moyamoya, bypass, carotid stenosis, AVMs, cavernous malformations, dural AV fistulas — and skull base surgery. He completed Temple neurosurgery residency plus endovascular and cerebrovascular/skull base fellowships. Claims show him performing LITT on Monteris NeuroBlate for a small number of brain-metastasis cases, indicating incidental/emerging tumor-ablation exposure alongside his vascular core. His publication record centers on middle meningeal artery embolization for subdural hematoma and cerebrovascular case reports.
training: Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University (MD) · Neurosurgery residency Temple University Hospital (2015–2022) · Fellowships: Endovascular Surgical Neuroradiology, Temple University Hospital (2021–2022); Cerebrovascular & Skull Base Surgery, Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell (2022–2023) · Dual open + endovascular cerebrovascular pedigree.
litt_exposure: Present but low-volume. Claims show NeuroBlate LITT for brain metastases (mets_rn=3). LITT is adjacent to, not central to, his cerebrovascular/endovascular wheelhouse.
wheelhouse: Cerebrovascular (open + endovascular): aneurysms, SAH, moyamoya, bypass, carotid stenosis, AVM/cavernoma, dural AV fistula; skull base surgery.
kol_note: Early-career; not yet a KOL. Publishing actively in cerebrovascular/endovascular topics but no LITT thought-leadership footprint.

name: Kadir Erkmen
identity: Kadir Erkmen, MD, FAANS — Professor and Vice Chairman of Neurosurgery, Director of Cerebrovascular Surgery, and Neurosurgery Residency Program Director, Lewis Katz School of Medicine / Temple University Hospital, Philadelphia PA. Packet NPI null; identity confirmed via Temple Health directory and ResearchGate. Development target.
bio: Kadir Erkmen is a senior cerebrovascular and skull base neurosurgeon and a major institutional leader at Temple — Vice Chairman, Director of Cerebrovascular Surgery, and Residency Program Director — and a longstanding Castle Connolly Top Doctor. His practice centers on cerebral aneurysms (clipping/coiling), AVMs, carotid disease, and complex skull base tumors including meningiomas; his published work is in skull base approaches and vascular neurosurgery. He is not a LITT operator: no claims and no LITT footprint, and his open vascular/skull base focus sits outside laser ablation. His strategic value is as a high-influence gatekeeper, referrer, and trainer of residents rather than as a device user.
training: University of Maryland School of Medicine (MD) · Neurosurgery residency Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Children's Hospital, Harvard Medical School · Fellowship in skull base & vascular neurosurgery, University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences · Strong pedigree (Harvard/BWH residency + dedicated skull base/vascular fellowship).
litt_exposure: No evidence. Vascular/skull base open-surgery focus; no LITT claims and no laser-ablation footprint.
wheelhouse: Cerebrovascular surgery (aneurysm clipping, bypass, AVM, carotid), complex skull base tumors and meningiomas; residency education and departmental leadership.
kol_note: High-influence academic KOL: Professor, Vice Chairman, Director of Cerebrovascular Surgery, and Residency Program Director; Castle Connolly Top Doctor since 2014. Publishes in skull base/vascular neurosurgery; shapes trainee practice patterns.

candidacy.assessment: Low direct-LITT affinity, high strategic value — cultivate as an influencer/gatekeeper rather than an operator.
candidacy.rationale: Erkmen is a vascular/skull base surgeon with no evidence of laser ablation, so he is unlikely to become a personal NeuroBlate user. But as Vice Chairman, Director of Cerebrovascular Surgery, and Residency Program Director he controls departmental direction, referral routing, and how residents are trained — the exact levers that grow (or starve) a LITT program. Development value lies in relationship-building and steering appropriate deep/eloquent or recurrent tumor cases toward NeuroBlate colleagues (Shepard) and toward the epilepsy service (Kasoff), plus embedding LITT in resident exposure. Competitive note: no Visualase/Medtronic attachment observed, so no incumbent to displace.
